page: Vultr vhf-4c-16gb is a virtual server belonging to the High Frequency Compute family. It features an Intel x86_64 architecture with 4 shared vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with Hyper-Threading enabled. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and includes 384 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark results indicate average performance across several standard workloads, alongside notable bottlenecks. The server achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 2411.16 and a multi-core score of 8740.87, both falling within the middle 50% of tested instances. However, memory subsystem performance drops significantly under heavy load; while small-block cached read bandwidth is strong at 497.33 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths are weak, measuring 35.47 GB/sec and 17.49 GB/sec respectively. Similarly, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang are positioned in the bottom 25% of benchmarks.

Because the CPU resources are shared rather than dedicated, this instance offers a cost-effective option for workloads that do not require sustained, peak CPU utilization. The bundled 384 GB NVMe SSD storage provides high local capacity relative to the compute tier, though database operations and static web serving throughput are benchmarked as weak. This server is best suited for general-purpose applications, text processing, light Redis deployments, and development environments that benefit from fast local storage but can tolerate shared CPU scheduling.
description: Vultr vhf-4c-16gb is a shared-CPU virtual server from the High Frequency Compute family, configured with 4 x86_64 Intel vCPUs, 16.0 GB of RAM, and 384 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmarks show average single-core and multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2411.16 and a PassMark CPU score of 7697.28. However, the instance exhibits weak performance in large-block uncached memory bandwidth, multi-threaded decompression, and database operations. Given its shared CPU allocation, the server represents a budget-friendly option for workloads requiring a balance of memory and local storage without sustained CPU demands. It is suitable for general-purpose hosting, text processing, Redis caching, and non-production development environments.
